```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

H1: The perceived morality of infidelity (IV) will effect willingness to marry without love (DV).

H2: Sex (categorical IV) will affect time spent dressing well (DV).

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
###JK: Use a project-relative path so the script can run on another computer. ###
# The current path points to a folder on your own computer.
# Replace the read.csv() line below with:
# raw <- read.csv("lab02_files/data_doctored.csv")
###  End of comment ###

raw <- read.csv("~/R Studio/PSY 221A/PSY221A-HW/lab02_files/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows

dim(raw)
head(raw)
str(raw)

#make data with ID, sex at birth, two morality items, time spent on dressing, and love opinion would you marry; keep raw unchanged

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId","Sex_birth","infmoral_sex","infmoral_emo","Love_would_you_marry_1","Time_A_dress_1")]


```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))
#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)
#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))
#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])
#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```


## 3. Recode sex at birth

```{r sex_at_birth}
# codebook: 0 = Male, 1 = Female, 2 = Intersex
table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
#turn Sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex
data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth, 
                         levels=c(0,1,2),
                         labels=c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

```


## 4. Overall Perceived Morality

```{r percMoral}
#group two infmoral_sex and infmoral_emo
summary(data$infmoral_emo)
summary(data$infmoral_sex)
table(data$infmoral_sex, useNA="ifany")
table(data$infmoral_emo, useNA="ifany")

percMoralVars <- c("infmoral_sex","infmoral_emo")
# calculate the 
data$percMoral <- rowMeans(data[,c("infmoral_sex","infmoral_emo")], na.rm = FALSE)
summary(data$percMoral)

```


## 5. Validate time spent dressing well
```{r Time_A_dress_1}
# taking a look at the variable
table(data$Time_A_dress_1,useNA="ifany")
# check for NAs, blanks
sum(is.na(data$Time_A_dress_1))
sum(data$Time_A_dress_1=="",na.rm=TRUE)
# check for empty records
missingTime <- which(is.na(data$Time_A_dress_1))
print(data[missingTime,])
# removing the known empty NAs

###JK: Do not remove missing dressing-time responses from the shared data table. ###
# Dressing time is needed for H2, but it is not needed for H1, which uses infidelity morality and willingness to marry without love.
# This line also removes 12,065 people who have the H1 responses you need.
###  End of comment ###

data <- data[!is.na(data$Time_A_dress_1),]
#double-checking that the stored data values are within the bounds of reason (time can only be measured 0-360)
sum(data$Time_A_dress_1 <0, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(data$Time_A_dress_1 >360, na.rm = TRUE)
#make h2Data with ID, Sex_birth, and time spent dressing
table(data$Time_A_dress_1)
h2Data <- data[!is.na(data$Time_A_dress_1) & !is.na(data$Sex_birth), c("ResponseId","Sex_birth","Time_A_dress_1")]
# check the h2Data
dim(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
summary(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
table(h2Data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
range(h2Data$Time_A_dress_1)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
# looks good!!! yay coding
```

## 6. Validate willingness to marry

```{r matrimonial directedness}
# taking a look at the variable
table(data$Love_would_you_marry_1,useNA="ifany")
# check for NAs, blanks
sum(is.na(data$Love_would_you_marry_1))
sum(data$Love_would_you_marry_1=="",na.rm=TRUE)
# check for empty records
missingWillingness <- which(is.na(data$Love_would_you_marry_1))
print(data[missingWillingness,])
# removing the known empty NAs
data <- data[!is.na(data$Love_would_you_marry_1),]
#double-checking that the stored data values are within the bounds of reason (measurement is 0-100)
sum(data$Love_would_you_marry_1 <0, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(data$Love_would_you_marry_1 >100, na.rm = TRUE)
#make h1Data with ID, perceived morality of infidelity, and willingness to marry
table(data$Love_would_you_marry_1)
h1Data <- data[!is.na(data$Love_would_you_marry_1) & !is.na(data$percMoral), c("ResponseId","Love_would_you_marry_1","percMoral")]
# I want to change the names of the data

###JK: Renaming these columns makes the later checks using their original names stop working. ###
# After this line, h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1 and h1Data$percMoral return NULL because those names no longer exist.
# Their range() checks then return Inf and -Inf, rather than checking your actual scores.
# The simplest fix is to remove the names(h1Data) line below and keep the original column names.
# Use var_label() to provide readable descriptions instead.
# Then these checks will work:
# range(h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1)
# range(h1Data$percMoral)
# Willingness should range from 0 to 100, and the morality mean should range from 1 to 7; please update the final-check comment accordingly.
###  End of comment ###

names(h1Data) <- c("ResponseId","Willingness to marry","Perceived morality")
# check the h1Data
dim(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
summary(h1Data)
```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h2Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
table(h2Data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
range(h2Data$Time_A_dress_1)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h1Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
range(h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1)
range(h1Data$percMoral)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
library(codebook)

###JK: The H1 labels are swapped, and the stated missing-data rule does not match your calculation. ###
# The columns are ID, willingness to marry, and perceived morality, but the labels below put morality before willingness.
# Your rowMeans(..., na.rm=FALSE) requires both morality items, whereas the current label says at least one response is enough.
# Replace the H1 label assignment below with:
# var_label(h1Data) <- c(
#   "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
#   "Willingness to marry without love: 0=Definitely would not, 100=Definitely would.",
#   "Perceived wrongness of infidelity: mean of infmoral_sex and infmoral_emo; both responses required. Items range from 1=Not at all wrong to 7=Extremely wrong. No reversal; higher scores indicate greater perceived wrongness."
# )
###  End of comment ###

var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Perceived morality of infidelity: mean of available perceived morality of infidelity questions, each 1=Not at all wrong 7=Extremely; no reverse coding; at least one valid response required", "Willingness to marry without love/matrimonial directedness; 0-100 with 0 representing that they would not marry and 100 representing they absolutely would"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Sex at birth: original codes 0=Male, 1=Female, 2=Intersex; now stored as a factor",
  "Daily time spent dressing well; 0-360 questionnaire with 360 representing 6 hours or more; zero is valid"
)
```

H2 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and six
allocations between 0 and 30 that total 30. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)
```

H1 includes participants with an ID, perceived morality (infmoral_sex and infmoral_emo), and willingness to marry without love.

```{r h2_codebook}

###JK: Please update the H2 inclusion description above the codebooks. ###
# The sentence about six allocations totaling 30 is left over from the example and does not describe your H2.
###  End of comment ###

#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)
```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
